questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Before receiving sedation, a client says, “I signed the form, but I still do not understand why this operation is needed.” What should the RN do?
choices: Pause preparation and ask the proceduralist to clarify before proceeding
Explain all surgical risks independently and proceed
Give the sedative so the client can relax
Ask a family member to sign a second form
questions.explanation: Consent requires informed, voluntary participation before sedation. The proceduralist provides the procedure-specific explanation; the RN pauses, advocates, and verifies understanding.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which finding requires resolution during the final surgical time-out?
choices: The consent says left knee while the schedule says right knee
The client wore glasses during the preoperative interview
The room temperature is comfortable
The client practiced coughing exercises
questions.explanation: A site discrepancy is a critical wrong-site risk. The team must stop and resolve it before the procedure begins.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A sponge count is incorrect as closure begins. What is the circulating RN's priority action?
choices: Notify the surgeon immediately and initiate the count-discrepancy protocol
Document the count as correct to avoid delay
Wait until the client reaches PACU
Assume the sponge was discarded with trash
questions.explanation: An incorrect count must be communicated and reconciled before closure according to the retained-item protocol, including systematic search and imaging when required.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which preoperative hair-removal plan best supports surgical-site infection prevention?
choices: Remove hair only if necessary, using an approved clipper method
Shave the operative site with a razor the night before
Use a razor immediately before every procedure
Remove hair from the entire body for consistency
questions.explanation: Routine hair removal is avoided. When required, approved clipping causes fewer skin microabrasions than razor shaving and follows facility timing and technique.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: In PACU, a client is difficult to arouse, snores, and has shallow respirations at 6/min while SpO₂ is 95% on oxygen. What is the priority?
choices: Support the airway and ventilation and summon assistance
Give another opioid for possible pain
Rely on the oxygen saturation and continue observation
Offer oral fluids to improve alertness
questions.explanation: Supplemental oxygen can preserve saturation despite dangerous hypoventilation. Airway opening, ventilatory support, help, and protocol-directed reversal take priority.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which intraoperative change is an early warning of malignant hyperthermia?
choices: Unexpected rapidly rising end-tidal carbon dioxide with tachycardia and rigidity
Mild postoperative thirst
A small stable bruise at the IV site
Gradual return of consciousness
questions.explanation: Unexpected rising carbon dioxide, tachycardia, rigidity, acidosis, and hyperkalemia may precede extreme fever. The malignant-hyperthermia protocol and dantrolene are time critical.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A postoperative client becomes tachycardic and hypotensive with cool skin and increasing abdominal distention despite little drainage on the dressing. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Internal hemorrhage with shock is possible
The small dressing stain excludes bleeding
These findings prove uncomplicated pain
This is expected after every abdominal surgery
questions.explanation: External drainage can underestimate internal blood loss. The hemodynamic and abdominal changes require immediate assessment, circulatory support, and surgical escalation.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: During sterile setup, the RN sees fluid soak through a wrapped sterile package. What should the RN do?
choices: Treat the package as contaminated and replace it
Cover the wet area with a sterile towel
Use the contents if the chemical indicator changed
Allow the package to air-dry on the field
questions.explanation: Moisture can compromise the barrier and permit contamination. Uncertain or compromised packaging is removed rather than covered or dried for use.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client coughs and abdominal organs protrude through a surgical incision. Which action is appropriate?
choices: Call for urgent surgical help and cover the tissue with sterile saline-moistened dressings per protocol
Push the organs gently back into the abdomen
Apply a dry tight pressure dressing and ambulate the client
Offer food while awaiting routine rounds
questions.explanation: Evisceration is a surgical emergency. Reduce wound tension, cover and protect exposed tissue according to protocol, keep the client NPO, and never attempt reinsertion.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which finding best supports safe discharge after ambulatory anesthesia?
choices: The client meets validated airway, vital-sign, consciousness, pain, nausea, bleeding, mobility, and transportation criteria
A fixed amount of time has elapsed despite new hypotension
The client can state their name but has repeated apnea
A discharge score is adequate even though bleeding is increasing
questions.explanation: Discharge uses validated criteria and clinical judgment. An unstable airway, circulation, bleeding pattern, or other concerning finding overrides elapsed time or a score.
